question: AP and AQ are two tangents drawn to a circle with center O from an external point A. If ∠PAQ = 40°, then ∠POQ is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle subtended by the two tangents at an external point and the angle subtended by their respective radii at the center are supplementary.

⇒ ∠POQ + ∠PAQ = 180°

⇒ ∠POQ + 40° = 180°

⇒ ∠POQ = 180° − 40° = 140°

**∴ The correct answer is 140°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 ∠PAQ + ∠POQ = 180°

**Given:**

∠PAQ = 40°

AP and AQ are tangents to the circle with center O.

**Formula Used:**

The radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent at that point.

The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

**Calculations:**

⇒ OP ⊥ AP and OQ ⊥ AQ

⇒ ∠OPA = 90° and ∠OQA = 90°

⇒ In quadrilateral APOQ,

⇒ ∠PAQ + ∠OPA + ∠OQA + ∠POQ = 360°

⇒ 40° + 90° + 90° + ∠POQ = 360°

⇒ 220° + ∠POQ = 360°

⇒ ∠POQ = 360° − 220°

⇒ ∠POQ = 140°

**∴ The correct answer is 140°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Tangents Property

The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal. Hence, AP = AQ.

Angle Bisector Property

The line segment joining the external point to the center of the circle bisects the angle between the tangents. Hence, ∠OAP = ∠OAQ.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Formation

The quadrilateral formed by the two tangents and the two corresponding radii (APOQ) is always a cyclic quadrilateral because the sum of its opposite angles (∠OPA and ∠OQA) is 180°.
